Integrations & Automation

Standard where it fits. Custom where it matters.

We start with established processes and standard ERP capabilities. When a business requirement needs a different workflow, we document the gap and agree on a customization or integration before building it.

    Map workflows and identify the outcomes the first release must support.

Insights

Prepare for ERP implementation

Document your current workflows and exceptions. Assign owners for master data, opening balances and testing. Choose a narrow first release and define what must be true before it can go live.

Decide between ERP and custom software

Start with standard ERP for common processes such as finance and inventory. Use a scoped custom app for distinctive workflows, and specify how data will move between the two.

Prepare data for migration

List the records needed at launch. Remove duplicates, agree on ownership and reconcile opening balances in a rehearsal before final migration.

Frequently asked questions

Can implementation be phased?

Yes. Agree on the modules, dependencies and readiness criteria for each release, then validate the first release before adding scope.

Can we keep systems that already work?

Yes. Identify system owners and the data that must flow between applications before choosing an integration approach.

What affects delivery time?

Scope, data readiness, integrations and stakeholder availability affect the schedule. Discovery is where those dependencies are mapped.

What should your systems do better?

Share the workflows, data and teams you need to connect. We’ll use that context to scope the next step.
